transcript.content:
I've analyzed the issue thoroughly. The problem is in `yt_dlp/YoutubeDL.py`, specifically in the `process_video_result` method around lines 2739-2742.

When a user runs `yt-dlp --list-subs` on a YouTube video that has only automatic captions (no manually uploaded subtitles), the output shows:

1. First: "Available automatic captions for [video]:" — listing all the auto-generated caption tracks
2. Then: "[video] has no subtitles" — because there are no *manual* subtitles

This contradictory output confuses users into thinking yt-dlp can't handle automatic captions. The root cause is that the code at lines 2740-2742 unconditionally calls `self.list_subtitles(info_dict['id'], subtitles, 'subtitles')` even when `subtitles` is empty — and the `__list_table` method (line 3768) turns that into a "[video] has no subtitles" message.

The fix is to conditionally display the "subtitles" section only when regular subtitles exist, or when neither automatic captions nor subtitles exist (to still show the "no subtitles" message for videos with no caption data at all). This is a change to the logic flow in `process_video_result`.
